teaser: A walkthrough from a spreadsheet CRM to one Drive folder per person, worked by Claude under a six-line policy, with five exercises, before any vault is needed.
core_idea: The jump from a spreadsheet CRM to the agents' vault-per-person memory is too high in one step and does not need to be: the row becomes a Google Drive folder with a record, an append-only ledger, the messages word for word, the notes and a summary the agent writes; the agent is a Claude Project connected to Drive and Gmail whose instructions are a six-line behaviour policy carried over unchanged from ours, draft never send, append never rewrite, stay in the folder; the migration is one afternoon, five exercises from a question to a campaign form the habit, two predictable mistakes are fixed by policy lines, and the vault is the later step whose shape the folders already have.

nodes.label: The jump is too high in one step
nodes.summary: From a customised spreadsheet to a vault per person with hashes and a graph; the folder is the step between.

nodes.label: The record is what happened, not the row
nodes.summary: In a folder the summary is derived from everything kept as it happened; in a spreadsheet the row is the summary you typed.

nodes.label: One folder, five documents
nodes.summary: Record, Ledger, Messages, Notes, and a Summary the agent writes and nobody edits by hand; the same shape as the agents' vault minus hashes and graph.

nodes.label: A Claude Project whose instructions are the policy
nodes.summary: Six lines: draft never send; read Contacts and Gmail, write only into a person's folder; append never rewrite; every fact names its source; ask before a new folder; report in one line.

nodes.label: Told, not enforced, so report
nodes.summary: Gmail drafting is enforced; the rest is told; the one-line report is the twin that lets you check, and a seat per agent makes the rest settings.

nodes.label: One afternoon
nodes.summary: Export the sheet, make the folders, fill each record from the mail the agent can read, correct once, generate the summaries; nothing is retyped again.

nodes.label: Five exercises
nodes.summary: Ask, prepare, draft, debrief, campaign: one message each, in order, over the first week.

nodes.label: Two predictable mistakes
nodes.summary: A fact without a source, and a summary that drops something; both fixed by a policy line and by fixing the source, never the summary.

nodes.label: When to move to a vault
nodes.summary: A second agent must read it, the operator must not, or the record must carry between tools; the move is a copy and the policy does not change.

nodes.label: Written to be sent
nodes.summary: The RiskMandate agent sends it with four substitutions: names, plan, three real contacts, the topic they sell.

quotes.text: The Summary is a view; the Record is the truth.
quotes.why: The rule that keeps the summary honest.

quotes.text: From then on, the rule is that nothing is retyped.

figures.caption: The row becomes a folder with four documents and one the agent writes; the agent is a Claude Project whose instructions are the policy; the five exercises below the line are the first week.
